title: The DSK Group Real Estate Fraud, Pune
dek: Pune-based builder D.S. Kulkarni's DSK Group collected deposits from roughly 33,000 investors and fixed-deposit holders promising good returns, then defaulted in 2016. Police allege a Rs 2,043 crore fraud across nine group companies, with a 37,000-page chargesheet and the arrest of serving and former Bank of Maharashtra chiefs for allegedly enabling loans to the group.

heroStat.label: alleged fraud across nine DSK Group companies, per Pune Police's Economic Offences Wing chargesheet, affecting roughly 33,000 investors and depositors

promise.quote: DSK Group's various companies solicited fixed deposits and investments from the public, including retail depositors, promising attractive fixed returns to be repaid on maturity alongside completion of the group's real estate projects.
promise.madeBy: D.S. Kulkarni (Deepak Sakharam Kulkarni), Chairman and Managing Director, DSK Group, and his wife Hemanti Kulkarni
promise.role: Founder and chief of DSK Group, a diversified Pune-based conglomerate with real estate, automobile, and other businesses
promise.context: This reflects the general fixed-deposit solicitation model reported across multiple DSK Group companies over several years, rather than a verified quotation from a specific deposit scheme's own paperwork, which this entry has not reviewed directly.

target.description: That depositors and investors who placed fixed deposits or investments with DSK Group companies would be repaid the promised principal and returns on maturity, as required of any regulated deposit-taking scheme.
target.standard: The Maharashtra Protection of Interest of Depositors (in Financial Establishments) Act, 1999 (MPID Act), and ordinary IPC provisions on cheating (Section 420) and criminal breach of trust (Section 406).

reality.description: DSK Group defaulted on repayments to fixed-deposit holders starting around October 2016, triggering complaints from thousands of depositors. Pune Police's Economic Offences Wing (EOW) subsequently arrested D.S. Kulkarni and his wife Hemanti from Delhi on 17 February 2018 and booked them under the MPID Act along with IPC sections for cheating and criminal breach of trust. In May 2018, the EOW filed an extensive chargesheet (reported at roughly 37,000 pages) alleging a Rs 2,043.18 crore fraud spread across nine DSK Group firms and about 33,000 investors/depositors, broken down as roughly Rs 1,083.7 crore in deposit/loan fraud, Rs 711.36 crore in fraud linked to banks and non-banking financial institutions, Rs 111.35 crore in debenture-related fraud, and Rs 136.77 crore tied to a Phursungi land purchase. In June 2018, the EOW separately arrested Bank of Maharashtra's then-CMD Ravindra Marathe, former CMD Sushil Muhnot, an executive director, and a zonal manager, alleging they had sanctioned loans to DSK Group in violation of banking norms. This entry's research, limited by an exhausted web-search budget during preparation, could not confirm the case's most current (2023-2026) trial status, any conviction, or final asset-recovery figures for depositors.

verdict.summary: This is a substantiated, chargesheeted case of large-scale deposit fraud: Pune Police's EOW has formally alleged, via a detailed 37,000-page chargesheet, that DSK Group and its promoters defrauded roughly 33,000 depositors of over Rs 2,000 crore, and separately arrested senior bank officials over related loan sanctions. Because this entry's research was cut short by an exhausted search budget, it cannot confirm whether these charges have since resulted in conviction, acquittal, or continued trial — that remains an open, unverified question.
verdict.reasoning: The 2016-2018 events (default, arrests, chargesheet, bank-official arrests) are corroborated by multiple contemporaneous Business Standard and other reports. However, this entry could not update the case's status beyond mid-2018 due to search-tool limits encountered during research, which is a significant gap given the case is now several years old.
